A.explanation: Larger p.d. gives larger current and more heating, so the metal filament gets hotter and its resistance $R = V/I$ increases.

B.explanation: More incident light releases more charge carriers in the LDR, so its resistance decreases, not increases.

C.explanation: At constant temperature an ohmic metallic conductor has constant resistance, so $V/I$ stays the same as current changes.

D.explanation: For the NTC thermistor used in this syllabus, higher temperature releases more carriers so resistance decreases.

hints: Look at what happens to the temperature of the filament lamp when the p.d. across it and the current through it both increase.
Recall how resistance of a metal depends on temperature because hotter ions vibrate more and scatter electrons.
Check the opposite trends for the other devices: light intensity for the LDR and temperature for the NTC thermistor both release more charge carriers.
walkthrough: Identify the changing condition for each component: heating of the filament by increased p.d., more light on the LDR, more current at fixed temperature, and heating of the thermistor.
Recall that resistance is defined by $R = V/I$ and that for a metal, resistance increases with temperature due to increased lattice vibrations and electron scattering.
For the filament lamp, increasing p.d. increases power $P = IV$, so the filament temperature rises markedly and its $I$-$V$ curve flattens.
This means $V/I$ gets larger, so the filament resistance increases with p.d.
By contrast, increased light on an LDR and increased temperature of an NTC thermistor both decrease resistance, and an ohmic conductor at constant temperature keeps constant $R$.
Therefore only the filament lamp shows an increase in resistance. This is option A
